note.item: For template authors: a template override of a document's lines or of its tax summary and totals (html/layouts/com_alfa/documents/partials/lines.php or taxes_totals.php in the administrator template) made from an earlier version keeps printing every document's amounts with a comma for decimals and a point for thousands, whatever the document's language, and Joomla does not flag such an override as outdated. Copy the 2.2.2 layout again and redo your changes, or in your copy read the document's separators with DocumentRenderer::separators() and pass them to DocumentMoney::formatter() and DocumentMoney::unitFormatter(), as the shipped layouts do.

For template authors: a product with no price applying reaches a template with its price null ($item->price), as the price layout already reads it, and core's add to cart slot is handed no layout (an empty layout name, which renders nothing). An override of the price layout or of the add to cart that reads the price must treat null as no price, not as zero.

The update rebuilds, in the background (Tools > Tasks), the product list prices of the products whose minimum quantity is above 1, which the list now reads at that quantity. Until that ends, the price filters and the price sort may still use such a product's price for one piece, or leave it out when its prices begin at its minimum; they are right once the rebuild ends.

For template authors: every product the storefront draws carries $item->sellsOnline, false in catalogue-only mode. Then the product page (item/default.php) and the catalogue card (items/default_item.php, and the items module's default_card.php) draw a plain block instead of their buy form and ask for none of its scripts (the variant, recalculate, add to cart, showon and validate scripts), and the product's fields arrive in the buy form's slot as plain lists (the layout item.fields_readonly, overridable in html/layouts/com_alfa/item/). An override made before 2.2.2 keeps its form and its scripts in the mode but sells nothing; one condition on $item->sellsOnline brings it to the new shape.

For template authors: the add to cart card (cart/added.php) has a third outcome, held (data-outcome="held"), drawn when nothing was added because the cart already holds the available quantity, and every card is handed that sentence as notice, which the added card also shows when the quantity was cut to the stock; a card that carries it has data-notice on its root, and the script shows such a card even when a cart drawer claims the add. An override made before 2.2.2 draws the held answer as a rejected add, its title "The item could not be added to the cart" over the notice, and a cut add's card with no notice and no data-notice, so a cart drawer claiming the add keeps it away and, with the confirmation card off, the card shows with no word of the cut; copy the 2.2.2 layout again, or draw $displayData['notice'], as the card's sentence when there is no line and under the title when there is one, with data-notice on the root of a card that draws it.

fix.item: Invoices, credit notes, receipts, delivery notes and every other sales document print their numbers the way the document's own language writes them: the amounts, the quantities and the tax rates. An English document prints 1,234.56, a quantity of 1,200 or 2.5 and a rate of 15.5%; a Greek one prints 1.234,56, 1.200 or 2,5 and 15,5%. Before, every document printed amounts and quantities with a comma for decimals and a point for thousands whatever its language, and rounded each rate to two decimals (8.875% printed 8,88%). A rate now prints with all its decimals (up to three). Only how the numbers are written changes: the amounts stored, the totals and how they are worked out, and the figures the REST API returns stay the same. A document issued before the update shows the new way of writing the next time it is printed, downloaded or e-mailed; a Greek document whose rates are whole numbers prints exactly as before. The back office's own screens keep showing a document's money as they did.

Clear Data of an extension that leaves a database transaction open: what the extension held for after a commit is discarded with that transaction, instead of running at the next save in the same request, and on the PDO driver the connection no longer counts a transaction the database has already ended. The thumbnails request, the document replacement preview and the inventory's integrity hold close their transactions through the same helper.

A product with no price for the shopper shows no price and no add to cart, on its page, on a catalogue card and in the items module, and cannot be added to a cart: no price row applies to their currency, place and customer group at the quantity it opens with or at any larger quantity. Before, it showed 0,00 and could be bought at zero. Its cart line, if it lost its price after it was added, says so, counts in no total and is refused at checkout. A product whose prices begin at a larger quantity than it opens with shows no price at that quantity and keeps its add to cart, and the cart says from which quantity it is priced. In the order builder such a product is added and waits for a custom price; the order popup and the REST API's order lines add it only with a custom price. The catalogue API publishes the price as null for both, the price filters leave them out and the price sort lists them after the products with a price. The setup checklist names the products whose minimum quantity no price row covers, whether their prices begin above it or all end below it. Every surface prices a product at the quantity it opens with, its minimum quantity, as the catalogue cards did: the product page (unless the shopper states a larger quantity), a card redrawn after a choice, and the price index, so a product sold from 10 pieces with prices from 10 shows its price for 10 and keeps its place in the price filters and the price sort. The price index holds the price of one piece at that quantity, as the card shows it, so the price filters, the price sort and the saving filters compare the cards' prices; the saving filters and the saving sort read the tax-included saving of one piece, as the price beside them is (a menu item whose "save at least" figure was set with the net saving in mind shows a different set of products).

The search module's results show each product's picture, as the catalogue's cards do: its first image, or the shop's placeholder for a product without one when the shop shows placeholders. Before, every result showed the product's name where a picture that does not exist was meant to be. A template override of the results (html/mod_alfa_search/result.php in the site template) is used.

A checkout field's name keeps its underscores: vat_number names the column vat_number (it became vat-number before). A field name is lowercase letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, at most 64 characters, with letters of other alphabets spelled in Latin letters of the site's default language, so the column is the same whoever saves the field; the field's description states the rule. A name that leaves no letters or is longer than 64 characters is refused before anything is saved, where before a long name failed to create its column after the field was saved. Existing columns keep their names.

The setup checklist titles each storefront menu item it creates in that item's own language, and an item for all languages in the site's default language (they took the language of whoever pressed the button); a title not yet translated reads in English. The Customer pages row says when the Create account page was not made because sign-ups are off in Users: Options, in every state of the row and right after it runs; a site that never saved that option is read as Joomla reads it, with sign-ups off, by the checklist and by Alfa's sign-up form alike (before, both read it as sign-ups on: the checklist made the sign-up page and the form created accounts, while Joomla's own sign-up refused them). For plugin authors: a setup check can carry a note, SetupCheck::note(), a sentence its row shows whether it is complete or not.

A new installation stores every Options setting that has a default with the default the Options form shows, and an update adds each such setting a shop's stored Options lack, whether or not the shop ever saved them, so what is stored and what the form shows agree. Sixteen were shown and not stored: Hide Subcategories When Filtered (Yes), Collapse Filter Options When Filtered (Yes), Guest checkout (Allowed), the added-to-cart Confirmation card (Show; Position Top Right; Vertical Offset 16 px; Horizontal Offset 16 px; Effect Slide; Close After 6 seconds), Search engine (Database search, built into Alfa Commerce), Downloads storage path (empty: alfa-downloads inside the site), Derived unit display precision (Auto), Images in the Card Slider (All) and Images Grid Columns (2). The storefront already read each of them with the same default, so nothing a shop sees changes, and a value a shop saved is kept. Reset to default now sets them to these defaults instead of removing them.

REST API: an order created over the API (POST v1/alfa/orders) is placed in the currency its id_currency names, when that is a currency the shop publishes, at the rate the checkout places orders at. An id_currency the shop does not publish (unpublished, unknown, or not an id) answers 400 naming the field, and nothing is created. Leaving id_currency out places the order in the shop's default currency, as before. Before, id_currency was ignored and every order was placed in the default currency.

REST API: an update of an order (PATCH v1/alfa/orders/{id}) that does not send the delivery details (alfa_form_fields), for example one that changes only customer_note, no longer asks for the fields the shop requires there. Before, on a shop with a required delivery field of its own, such an update answered 400 naming that field. Creating an order still needs every required field. An update that sends the delivery details needs the fields of the shop's own that it requires there, and a required field it leaves out keeps its stored value; the name, e-mail, phone, country, address, city and postcode are not asked on an update.

REST API: an update of an order (PATCH v1/alfa/orders/{id}) that sends some of the delivery or invoice details (alfa_form_fields, alfa_form_fields_billing) changes only the fields it sends; the others keep their values. Before, the details sent replaced the order's details whole: a city sent alone left the order's delivery details with only the city, and on a guest order a name sent without the e-mail also removed the customer's e-mail, so the order's status e-mails stopped. A PATCH that sends the invoice details with invoice_differs but not the delivery details now writes them; before, it answered 200 and wrote nothing. Invoice details (alfa_form_fields_billing) sent without invoice_differs, to a POST or a PATCH, are refused with 400 naming invoice_differs, and nothing is saved; before, they were dropped without a word. A PATCH that states invoice_differs 1 without the invoice details keeps the order's own invoice details as they are, and answers 400 naming alfa_form_fields_billing when the order has none; before, with the delivery details sent, it moved the order's invoice onto its delivery details. invoice_differs 0 on its own still invoices to the delivery details. The order screen, which sends the details whole, is unchanged.

The payment and shipment ledgers no longer show the shopper any of their messages on the storefront (a record that could not be locked, stored or found, a reference stored shortened, a failed side step); staff and API clients still read them, without the database's own text, and the orders log (com_alfa.orders) keeps them in full. Before, a payment page could show a technical line with the database's error text when another operation held the order.

After a filter or a change of page, the product list now always opens at its top, right under the shop's sticky header, and no longer draws a frame around the whole list. Before, the list was moved only when its top was out of sight, its top could end up hidden behind a sticky menu bar (with the sort and the page links), and in some templates a mouse click on a page link left a coloured box around the entire list. When the template does not give the header's height (--alfa-scroll-offset), the height is measured from what stays sticky or fixed at the top of the window, again where the scroll ends, so a header that becomes sticky only once the page scrolls is counted; a layer over the whole window (a cookie notice's backdrop, an open menu) is not. A page opened again by a reload or the back button keeps the place the shopper had. The list still takes the keyboard focus, so a keyboard or screen reader user lands on the results and hears how many products show; when none match, it now says so. A variant or a quantity changed in a product card moves nothing.

The checkout offers only the shipping methods that can carry the order with the details given so far. A method that serves every country and postcode can be chosen before any address is filled; one priced for particular countries or postcodes appears once the delivery country or the postcode is filled in, and when nothing can be chosen yet the list says what is needed. Before, every method was listed, and choosing one priced for particular countries with no country filled in was answered with "cannot carry this order (no delivery zone is configured for this destination)" and unchecked. A chosen method that stops serving a changed address is still unchecked with its reason.
Tools > Media: an image whose combination no longer exists is marked as an orphan and shown by the orphan filter, as Delete all orphans already counted it.

A price stored with more decimals than the currency, such as a net of 290.32258 brought over from another shop, is shown on the product page, the catalogue cards and the items module with the currency's decimals for one piece (290,32 €), and with a further decimal only where a larger quantity needs it to be shown truthfully. A price below the currency's smallest unit (0.004) and an agreed price still show their own decimals. The stored price does not change: the price filter, the API's amount and the price editor keep it exactly, and the API's formatted text is the one the storefront shows. Before, every stored decimal was shown (290,32258 €).

For shipping plugin developers: a parcel's settle (ShipmentsPlugin::settleAttempt(), the update builder's saveVerdict()) writes the plugin data staged on its builder with pluginData() and removePluginData() in the same write as the status, merged with the payload the row holds at that moment, and none of it when the row has already left the expected status. Before, it moved the status and left the staged keys unwritten.

Options, Currencies, Default Currency lists only the published currencies, and a saved value must be one of them: an unpublished default could be chosen, which left the setup checklist's Default currency step open and the shop's currency unresolved for every page that needs it. A shop whose default is no longer published sees "Select a currency" there, and Options are saved once a published currency is chosen.

The currency edit screen's Status can no longer take the store's default currency, or the last published currency, out of service (unpublished, archived or trashed): the save is refused with the sentence the currencies list's Unpublish, Archive and Trash give. A PATCH of a currency over the REST API is refused the same way.

Adding a product when the cart already holds every unit of it that is available answers with one notice, "Your cart already holds the available quantity (1).", adds nothing and leaves the add to cart button as it was. A request for more than is available adds what is and says so in one notice, "Added up to the available quantity (2).", on the add to cart card, which shows for it even with the confirmation card switched off or with the cart module opening its drawer on an add. The cart page's quantity change says the same sentences when the stock limits it, the order builder's Add popup says the first as a notice and stays open instead of "The item could not be added to the cart.", and the add's JSON answer carries the sentence as its message, the figure as available_quantity, when nothing was added what the cart holds as total_items and total_quantity, and cart_changed, true when a line was lowered to what the stock now holds although nothing was added, so the other cart surfaces on the page read again. The figure is what the cart holds of that stock afterwards. Before, the first answered "The item could not be added to the cart" with "The quantity was adjusted to the available stock.", which read as a failure of the product, and the card confirmed a cut request with no word about the cut. A product with no stock left and none of it in the cart is still refused as out of stock, and so is a quantity the stock cuts below the product's minimum while the cart holds none of that stock, no longer with the adjusted sentence beside it; with some of it in the cart, that cut says "Your cart already holds the available quantity (3).". The Options' Confirmation card texts and the cart module's note say that a card the stock limited still shows.

addition.item: For extension developers: onAlfaPricesChanged is also announced when a price period stored ahead of time begins (a price, a discount or a tax whose dates were set in advance), with the cause window (PricesChangedEvent::CAUSE_WINDOW): one change for each stored row whose final price moved at that moment, the period that ended as the old price. Nothing is written then, so the background work announces it at its first turn at least a minute after the moment (on a shop with visitors or cron, within about two minutes). It covers the periods the price index stores, at most eight per product, the nearest ones. Where the announcements have reached is kept in #__alfa_meta (prices.windows_announced_until), written by the installation, so nothing that began before it is announced.

Catalogue-only mode: Options, Cart, Online sales, Catalogue only. The storefront shows the products with their details, images and stock, and every product field as a plain list of its options with nothing to choose; no prices, no add to cart, no price filters or price sorts. The cart and the checkout show one sentence instead of the cart, the cart module shows nothing, and every storefront cart task and order is refused. Orders taken in the administrator or over the REST API, and orders already placed (their pages, downloads, payment returns and webhooks), are not affected; stored carts are kept and come back when selling is switched on again. The catalogue API publishes prices and option amounts as null. Switching online sales on or off, by the Options, Reset to default or Clear everything, drops the pages Joomla's page cache stored, so visitors see the shop as it is now; another extension's page cache, a server's or a CDN's cache, and pages kept in browsers under Use Browser Caching are purged by their own means. The setup checklist says when online sales are off.

The customers list shows each customer's Joomla account: Account (Enabled, Blocked or Awaiting activation, with the icons of Joomla's users list) and User groups (their titles), with a filter and a sort on the account state.
The customer's page says, above the button that opens the Joomla user, that the user groups, enabling or blocking the account, the password and the e-mail address are edited there.

The setup checklist lets a Super User ignore a recommended or optional step that is not done, such as Item fields on a shop whose products have no options, or Joomla mail on a test copy that must not send e-mail: Ignore on its row moves it under Ignored, at the end of the checklist and out of the count, and Show again brings it back. A required step cannot be ignored. The choice is the site's, the same for every administrator; a reset of the Options keeps it and Clear everything removes it. For plugin authors: a plugin's recommended or optional check can be ignored like core's and needs nothing for it; SetupCheck::ignorable() says whether a check can be, and the evaluated checklist marks each row ignored or not.

For payment plugin developers: every write of a buyer's visit can answer why it did not write. The builder's new saveWithVerdict() (a new row or a change), and PaymentsPlugin's new settleAttemptVerdict(), supersedeAttemptVerdict() and claimPendingAttemptVerdict(), answer a PaymentWriteVerdict: its kind (VERDICT_WRITTEN; VERDICT_REFUSED, a money or business rule refused it, permanent for the order as it stands; VERDICT_LOCK_NOT_TAKEN, another operation held the order, nothing was written, try again; VERDICT_WRITE_FAILED, the database refused the row, nothing was written; VERDICT_RACED, the row left the expected status first), a stable code for a refusal (REFUSAL_OVER_TOTAL, REFUSAL_OPEN_ATTEMPT, REFUSAL_REFERENCE_TAKEN and the others, re-exported on PaymentsPlugin as self::REFUSAL_*), a sentence for your log, the row, and for a money rule its figures. Decide on the kind, then the code; word the buyer's sentence in your own strings. save(), saveVerdict(), settleAttempt(), supersedeAttempt() and claimPendingAttempt() keep their answers.

For payment plugin developers: write your pending row first, with a reference you mint, through saveWithVerdict(), and call the provider only when it answers VERDICT_WRITTEN, with an idempotency key taken from the row. Written again with the same reference, the create answers the same row (existing true) and writes nothing; the reference on another row is refused with REFUSAL_REFERENCE_TAKEN. Read your own open attempt first (latestPendingPayment()) and resume, claim or close it; a gateway never closes another gateway's attempt.

Related products: a product's page can show other products after it, chosen on the product's new Related tab in the order you set, each picked from the products list in a window with its search and filters. A link goes one way: a product shows the products you add on its page, and shows on theirs only if you add it there too. The page shows only the related products the visitor may see in the listing, priced as the listing prices them, each with the listing's own card, at most 4 by default; the number, from 0 (none) to 12, and the part's version are set per product, category, menu item or in the Options (the Item tab). Save as Copy copies a product's related products; deleting a product removes it from every other product's related products; a product in the trash, unpublished or archived keeps its links and is not shown. The REST API's item record lists them as related, their ids in order, for reading: a create or change that sends related is refused with 422 and nothing is saved. A template override of the product page (item/default.php) shows the related products only where it loads the new part, default_related.php.

For payment plugin developers: unbookedProviderRefundsOfPayment($paymentId) on the base class reads, for one of your payments, the refunds your provider reports that the books do not hold, as the core reads them from your unbookedProviderRefunds(): which reserve their amount ('reserved'), which hold the refund block ('refunds'), and what could not be read ('unread'). Read only; another gateway's payment answers nothing. Never call it from your own unbookedProviderRefunds(): the core refuses that call and reads the payment as unread until the plugin is fixed.

Each payment method and shipping method can have one image, on its Image tab, chosen and stored as a manufacturer's image. The cart shows each method as its radio button, then its image, its title, the description the shop wrote and what its plugin adds; the product page shows the same without the radio button; the back office lists show the image beside the name. The image's alt text is the one written on its tile, else the method's title. The REST API publishes a method's image as medias and takes media on a write, as a manufacturer's. Tools, Media finds the image of a deleted method as an orphan.

change.item: For plugin authors: a product field extension changes the add to cart area of a catalogue card or of the product page only through its event's setCartLayout() and setCartChildLayout(). When its method fails, what it set is left out and the other fields keep theirs, and a change it writes straight onto the product's cart ($item->cart, $item->cartChildren) is not kept, whether its method fails or not. Before, such a change stayed: after a failure the card or the page could show the failed extension's button, or none, and the card could lose its Choose options link.

For plugin authors: System - Alfa Commerce Sync no longer carries a commented-out onAlfaProductAfterSave subscription and handler. Alfa Commerce announces no such event; an item's save is announced by onItemAfterSave.

For plugin authors: EmailService::orderNumber() takes the Order reader a payment or shipping plugin is handed, EmailService::orderNumber(order: $order), and gives the number the customer knows the order by. A plugin no longer needs Order::row(), which is not part of the plugin-facing API, to call it. Core's own code still passes the order row.

The cart, the cart rules, the translations, the price index, the item field filters and two install steps (moving the shipping options and repairing the saved layout choices) close their database transaction levels through Alfa Commerce's own transaction helper, so work held for after a commit (an announcement, a notice, a task) runs once the outermost transaction commits and never after a rollback. They closed them with the database driver alone; none of those levels held such work, so nothing was lost.

For extension developers: TransactionState::driver() narrows a connection to the database driver whose transaction levels Alfa Commerce keeps, and refuses any other; the cart, the price index, the item field projection and the inventory service use it once, when they are made. Nothing a shop sees changes.

For plugin authors: a field plugin whose contributions are the whole price of a product (a product that prices what the buyer fills in) states it with PriceContributionBuilder::suppliesBase(); a product with no price row is priced from such a contribution, and from no other: an option's, a combination's or a contribution's amount alone no longer prices a product that has no price row. PriceContribution gains suppliesBase and withSource().

For extension developers: PriceResult::isPriced() says whether a price applies at the quantity asked and pricedFrom() the smallest larger quantity from which one applies; a result with no price throws from its money getters instead of answering zero, so ask isPriced() first. VariantHelper::resolveAndPrice() answers the result as stated (the item carries it only when priced, and carries pricedFrom), CartHydrator::priceAt() and OrderModel::priceConfigIn() answer the result as stated, and AlfapricesField::chargedPrice() answers null for a variant with no price.

For plugin authors: in catalogue-only mode the product page's and the card's buy slots (BuyForm, NearAddToCart) hold no plugin surface, a field's or a feature plugin's alike, only core's read-only lists of the product fields, and the add to cart slot is none, whatever a plugin set; core sets them after the field events, the page's onItemDisplay and the listing's onItemsListPrepare. A plugin reads $item->sellsOnline to decide what it draws in the display slots.

For plugin authors: the checkout now asks every shipping method's plugin its onCalculateShippingCost question before listing the method, and lists only those that answer a price; keep that answer quick and free of side effects. The method's isSelected() is true only for the method the cart has chosen; for any other, the checkout reads only whether it can carry the cart, so a plugin that prices through an outside service can answer a listing on its own and call the service for the chosen method. When the delivery country or the postcode has not been given yet, costFromZones() refuses with one of core's own reasons, ShipmentsPlugin::REFUSAL_NEEDS_PLACE or REFUSAL_NEEDS_POSTCODE, worded by core, so a plugin needs no language key for them; pass that refusal on with setUnavailable($this->refusal()), and pass an empty string as the postcode when your postcode field is set but unanswered (null when you read none). The checkout then names what is needed instead of listing the method. Every field of the delivery details now reads the shipping methods again when it changes; a template override of the checkout form wraps the delivery fields in an element with the data-cart-delivery-fields attribute for this.

For extension developers: CartService::summary() is the cart module's reading, the lines and the totals with no offers (its offers are null), so no shipping method is asked to quote for a list on every page the module shows; the module and its quantity changes read it, so a template override of the module reads no offers. CartSnapshot::$shipmentId names the chosen shipping method on every reading.

The product page's payment and shipping methods show each method's title and description, drawn by Alfa: a method shown on product pages whose plugin draws nothing there now appears with them, and the description is printed as text (the Standard methods printed it as HTML).

For plugin authors: a payment or shipping plugin's product page layout (its item view) no longer draws a logo, the method's title or its description, which Alfa draws; it adds only its own content below them, and with nothing to add it sets no layout. The Standard payment and shipping plugins no longer ship a product page layout.

note.item: The update removes columns that nothing in Alfa Commerce reads: the coupon id, the coupon code, the invoice date and the invoice number of the orders (the invoice number with its key), the invoice id of the order lines, the parcels and the order's cart rules, and the e-mail subject and body columns of each language's order status table (the status e-mails are built from their parts and layout, which stay). No data a shop uses is in them. On MariaDB 10.6 and on MySQL 8.0.29 or later the removal changes only the tables' definitions, so it is immediate: measured with 100,000 orders, order lines, parcels and order cart rules, a few thousandths of a second per table on MariaDB 10.6 and under a twentieth of a second per table on MySQL 8.0. The orders' key on the invoice number is removed first, on its own, so that the orders' columns go immediately too: removed together, MySQL 8.0 takes about half a second for 100,000 orders. A MySQL server older than 8.0.29 rebuilds each table in place instead, at most about 1 second for 100,000 orders and 3 seconds in all for 100,000 rows in each of the four tables (measured as a full copy); saves go on meanwhile, and the update takes that much longer. Easylogic's own extensions were scanned and none of them reads these columns. A report or an extension of your own that reads them by name stops working; nothing else changes.

E-mail layout overrides are read from one place only: the default administrator template (administrator/templates/<template>/html/layouts/com_alfa, then the template it inherits from). An override kept in the site template's html/layouts/com_alfa folder, where the 2.2.0 Manual advised a copy for the e-mails the storefront sends, is no longer read after the update, and those e-mails then use the administrator template's override or Alfa Commerce's own layout. The update names each such file on the update page and in the maintenance log (com_alfa_maintenance.php). Copy such files into the administrator template before or with the update; the update moves and deletes nothing.

security.item: A thumbnail is made only from an image file inside the media folders (the Media folders of Joomla and Alfa Commerce's own image folder) whose type matches its extension. Before, a member of staff allowed to edit products, categories or manufacturers, or an API client with that right, could name any file the site can read (a backup, a log, the site's configuration file) as a thumbnail, and a copy of it, its extension kept, was published in the image folder (images/commerce by default) for anyone to download. A save that names such a thumbnail is now refused with a message and writes nothing, so the gallery keeps the thumbnails it had; the API answers 400 with the same reason; the Recreate thumbnails job names an image that breaks the rule in its report instead of copying it.

The update lists the files among the product images that are not images, with the media rows that name them, on the update page and in the media log (com_alfa_media.php in Joomla's log folder). Up to 2.2.0 such a file may be a copy of a site file published by the defect above. Nothing is deleted: look at each file and delete by hand those that are not yours to publish, then choose a new thumbnail for the rows named.

The search, items, easy articles and cart modules answer a request that sends a list where one value is expected (for example module_id[]=1) with "400 Bad Request" and a plain sentence. Before, such a request was answered with an error page that named a file on the server; the search module's address needs no form token.

A registration stores the customer's details exactly as the registration form checked them: each field's own rules and clean-up applied, and nothing kept for a field the form hid. Before, the values were taken from the submitted page as they came, on every account save, Joomla's own registration page included, so a required field could be left empty, a phone number kept unformatted, or a value stored that the form never offered. Details saved before are kept as they are.

A required customer details or registration field whose form field plugin is disabled, missing, or not available to the visitor (its Access is not Public) now stops the form with a message naming the field, instead of being left out and the order, account or details saved without it. This covers every form that asks for those fields: the checkout, the registration form, the customer's My details page, and the customer details and order forms staff use. An optional field in that state is left out, as before, and noted in the log. A new row of the setup checklist names each required field that not every visitor can fill in, with the details it is required in.

A request to the component's storefront pages or to its REST API that sends a list where one value is expected (for example id_line[]=1) is answered "400 Bad Request" with a plain sentence. Before, some storefront pages answered with an error page that named a file on the server.

Issuing a sales document now needs the Sales Documents: Create permission and voiding one the Sales Documents: Change State permission, checked by the document service itself whoever calls it. The screens and the API already asked for them; an extension that issues or voids documents is now held to the same rule. Automatic issue on a status change is the shop's own policy and asks no staff permission.

A request to the component's administrator screens and their tasks that sends a list where one value is expected (for example id[]=1) is answered "400 Bad Request" with a plain sentence, as the storefront and the REST API are. Before, some answered with an error page that named a file on the server. It needs a signed-in administrator.

With Joomla's System - Page Cache plugin on and System - Alfa Commerce Sync disabled, not installed or set to an Access that visitors who are not logged in do not hold, a visitor's cart page, with the checkout details typed and the coupon, and the cart module on every page were stored and shown to the next visitors. Alfa Commerce's own pages and modules now keep themselves out of the page cache whatever plugin is enabled: the cart page in every form (the cart, the checkout, the empty cart and the order pages), a product page opened to change a cart line, the cart module while it shows products, and every page priced in a currency or place of the visitor's own. A page whose cart module is empty stays cacheable. What remains without System - Alfa Commerce Sync: a shopper with products in the cart, or priced in a currency or place of their own, may be given a page stored from another visit, with an empty cart module or the shop's own prices; nothing of the other visitor is on it.

The page shown before payment and the order page shown after it now open only an order placed in this browser session, or one a payment gateway has confirmed through its own checked return. Before, a payment gateway extension that wrote the order its return named into the visitor's session before checking that the return was genuine let anyone point their own session at any order of the shop with one request to the payment return address: the order page after payment then showed that order, a guest's order with its details included, and the page before payment asked that order's gateway for a new payment page. Any other order is now refused: the visitor is sent to the cart with a message saying that a completed payment is recorded and its confirmation e-mail has the details, nothing of the order is shown, and the refusal is logged (com_alfa_orders.php in Joomla's log folder). A payment gateway built before 2.2.0 still works for the buyer who placed the order in the same session; when its return arrives in another session, the buyer lands on the cart with that message until the gateway's 2.2.0 package is installed.

fix.item: A registration refused by its checks (two passwords that differ, for example) is no longer shown to other visitors: with Joomla's System - Page Cache plugin on, the registration page re-filled with the name, username and e-mail typed was stored and shown to the next visitor who opened the registration page, with the password typed in its form. The page now keeps itself out of the page cache, the password typed is no longer kept at all, and the other fields typed re-fill only the page that shows the refusal, under Alfa Commerce's own session key, so Joomla's own registration page no longer receives them.

A visitor whose session holds a currency or a place of their own, set by a site's own code for Alfa Commerce's prices, is kept out of Joomla's System - Page Cache: every page priced for that visitor keeps itself out, and System - Alfa Commerce Sync also keeps that visitor from being shown a page stored for another. A listing stored with one visitor's currency was shown to the next visitor with that currency's prices.

The order page shown before payment, reached again by a reload or by Try again, keeps itself out of Joomla's System - Page Cache. With System - Alfa Commerce Sync disabled it could be stored and shown to the next visitor with the order's number.

The items module, showing a visitor's recently viewed products, keeps the page out of Joomla's System - Page Cache. Before, the page stored from one visitor's visit showed that visitor's recently viewed products to the next visitors.

The easy articles module, showing a visitor's recently read articles, keeps the page out of Joomla's System - Page Cache, with System - Alfa Commerce Sync enabled or not. Before, the page stored from one visitor's visit showed that visitor's recently read articles to the next visitors.

The items module refreshes its best sellers ranking as often as its option says, in minutes: the default 60 refreshes it every hour. Before, it kept the ranking 60 times longer (60 hours by default). An update also clears the module's stored ranking and listings, so nothing the version before computed stays.
REST API: a tax, discount or cart rule that does not exist answers 404, as every other resource does, instead of 500 (GET v1/alfa/taxes/{id}, discounts/{id} and cartrules/{id}).

REST API: a delete that is refused answers 409 with the reason, and nothing is deleted: an order status orders are in, or the last status holding a role, and a payment or shipping method that orders, payments, parcels, stored payment references or a payment method's shipping list still use. It answered 204 while the record stayed. The back office shows the same reason once.

Without the dompdf library (lib_dompdf), or a library it needs, a document's PDF answers 503 with a sentence that names the library, in the back office and over the REST API (GET v1/alfa/documents/{id}/pdf), instead of 500. The setup checklist has a new recommended row, PDF library for sales documents, that says how to restore it; status e-mails still go out without the PDF and log it.
REST API: POST v1/alfa/users refuses a Joomla user that does not exist, user 0 and a user who already has a customer record, with the reason (400). The administrator's customer form checks the same.

REST API: a payment or shipping method created without color or bg_color takes the colours its edit screen offers, and a customer group created without prices_display takes the price display Alfa Sync gives every new group; a group updated without it keeps its own. Each failed with a database message.
REST API: a new order status keeps its invoice rules (issues_doc_rules) when the request does not send issues_delivery_note; they were dropped and the status issued no documents.
REST API: PATCH v1/alfa/orders/{id} writes customer_note; it answered 200 and wrote nothing.
Creating an item, a form field, a place or a currency no longer writes PHP warnings to the log.

The stock step of a status change that fails (for example the database was briefly unreachable) is tried again with the shop's usual backoff, and if it keeps failing it shows in Tools > Tasks and in the notification bell. Before, it failed at once and nobody was told, while the order's stock stayed unmoved.

A stock movement that a stock extension refuses on purpose is no longer retried for ever: it is recorded as refused and its notice names the refusal. For an order, staff decide on the order, and a new status that changes the order's stock claim tries it again (a status that keeps the claim does not); for a document, the movement waits in Tools > Tasks, and only running that task again tries it, once the extension allows it. A stock movement that keeps failing for another reason is tried again with the waits the shop's task runner uses (1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours, 6 hours and 24 hours after each failure, about 33 hours in all), then waits for staff and its notice says so; a new status of an order tries that order's failed movement at once, and Apply outstanding stock movements in Tools > Database Sync tries every failed movement at once.

Saving a product is one step: its details, translations, images, prices, categories, manufacturers, who may see it, options, downloads, variants, stock and a move into the archive are all saved, or, if the save stops part way (for example the database was briefly unreachable), none of them is and staff are told that nothing was kept. Before, a save that stopped part way could leave the product with new details and old prices, or with no categories. The catalogue rebuild and the extensions told of the save hear of it only once it is complete. An image removed in the save has its files deleted only once the save is complete, so a save that stops keeps the image and its files; an image uploaded by a save that stops is left in the images folder, where the media maintenance page of Tools lists it under Untracked files on disk.

Saving a discount or a tax rule saves the rule and its scope (categories, manufacturers, places, customers, customer groups) in one step, and extensions told of the save read the scope as it was saved. Before, they were told before the scope was written.

A product or variant price for a country that was later deleted keeps its country: the price editor shows it as "#number (deleted)" with a note, and saving the product unchanged keeps it. Before, the editor showed "All" for such a row and saving the product turned that country's price into a price for every country. Setting such a row to every country is refused, naming the row, and deleting a country that price rows name says so, naming their products.

On a phone, Tools > Tasks, the orders list and an order's page fit the screen. Below 480 px a row of the background jobs list, of the orders list and of an order's payments, shipments, items, documents and reconciliation folds: its values wrap under one another, each named by its column (an extension's column by its own title), and its buttons take a line of their own under it. A background job's next-try date stays on one line. Before, at 360 px the orders list and an order's page were wider than the screen and scrolled sideways (on a test order with one payment and one shipment, 941 px and 1,182 px; in Greek 1,098 px and 1,584 px), and the jobs list's buttons were partly or wholly out of sight, behind a sideways scroll of 14 px in English and 116 px in Greek.

The result of a plugin action, a refused one included, shows its message above its Close or OK button. Before, on a phone, with the site's own messages above it, the button bar pinned to the bottom of the window covered the first lines of the message.

REST API: deleting a currency that orders, prices or places use, or an item field a product still uses, answers 409 with the reason, and nothing is deleted. It answered 204 while the record stayed. The back office shows the same reason once.

REST API: PATCH v1/alfa/orders/{id} with state answers 422 with the reason: over the API an order has no trash step and is deleted in one call, and its status changes through POST v1/alfa/orders/{id}/status. It answered 200 and wrote nothing.

REST API: a PATCH that leaves out a required name (one that changes only a category's or a manufacturer's state, for example) no longer answers 400 "Field required: Name"; the stored names are kept. A create without a name, and a PATCH that sends the name empty, are still refused.
REST API: the answer to a PATCH of a product's images shows them as saved; it showed them as they were before the save.
A carrier asking for the shipping method of a shipment whose method was deleted, or that has none, is handed nothing, instead of false or an empty new method; a failure reading it is logged.

A price calculation with a quantity list that leaves out one of the products, or gives one a quantity that is not a whole number of at least 1, is refused, naming the product, instead of failing with a PHP error or pricing that product at a quantity of 1 (or 2.5 as 2).

Saving a category tells the search and catalogue plugins about the change after the category's products have been updated and after the save is committed, so a plugin that reads a product then sees the new audience.
A stock allocation plugin is given who placed the order and why, as its interface promises, instead of an empty context; the allocation plugins are collected once per request.

When a plugin's check of an order fails at checkout, the shopper is told in plain words that the order could not be checked and was not placed, instead of only "Order placement failed", and the orders log (com_alfa_orders.php in Joomla's log folder) names the plugin and its failure; a plugin that refuses the order on purpose by throwing is read in its own words, as its rejection is. When Joomla does not load a plugin of the customer's cart for the member of staff placing the order, the order is still refused, naming that plugin, before any plugin checks it.

The notice of a document that could not be issued automatically says why, in the sentence staff read for that refusal when it has one (an order with no currency, for example), else the failure's own first line; a database error is named as one, its detail kept in the log.

E-mail layout overrides are read from the default administrator template whatever sends the mail (the storefront, the REST API, the console), the same template the order status's layout list offers; before, a mail sent from the storefront did not find them.
An order created with a shipping method needs an existing delivery address; one without is refused before anything is written. An order with no shipping method needs none.
Saving a cart rule, a payment method or a shipping method is one transaction, and the plugins told about the save hear it after the commit, with the translations, the conditions and the scope saved.

Updating from 2.1.x no longer warns "The scheduled tasks of plg_task_alfapricesets were not removed": the update removes those tasks itself before it uninstalls the plugin, and says once that the plugin was removed.

The Standard payment plugin's partial refund form offers at most what the order may still refund, so it no longer accepts a figure the refund then refuses (after a credit note settled to the customer's wallet).
A shopper whose order a stock extension refuses at placement reads the extension's own sentence. Before, the shopper read only "Order placement failed", and the reason was in the server log.

A stock movement whose process stopped before it finished (for example it ran out of time or memory) is tried again with the same waits and the same limit as a movement that failed, and after the last try it waits for staff, with the notice that says so. Before, it was tried again every five minutes with no limit.

REST API: a POST or PATCH of an item that carries its options, combinations, item field values or downloads (fields, options, combinations or informational, as the item read publishes them, or the item edit form's own keys for them, item_downloads among them) answers 422 naming them, and nothing is saved; they are edited on the item's page in the administrator. Before, the item was saved and those values reached the option, variant and download writers in a shape they do not read: a list sent as the read publishes it was taken by its positions, so its second entry could change the option whose value id is 1, and the edit form's keys (deleted_option_value_ids, for one) were obeyed.

REST API: a POST or PATCH of an item field that carries values or deleted_value_ids answers 422 naming them, and nothing is saved; a field's values are edited on its page in the administrator. Before, a value named by its id was saved under the field whatever field it belonged to, so another field's value, with the options and variants built on it, moved under this one, and deleted_value_ids deleted unused values of any field.

With System - Alfa Commerce Sync enabled, the dashboard cards and the setup checklist follow an Alfa Commerce extension from the next page on when it is installed, updated, uninstalled, enabled or disabled, whether that is done in the Plugins list, in Extensions: Manage or in the extension's own form. Before, a removed or disabled extension's card could still be drawn for up to 5 minutes, with untranslated texts and a link to a page that no longer exists, and the setup checklist kept its rows, or missed a new extension's rows, for up to 6 hours.

A discount or a tax scoped to a place now reaches every place inside it: a customer whose place is a region or a town of a country gets the country's discounts and taxes, as the shipping taxes of the same order already did. When several rules match, the rules scoped to places are ranked by nearness (the customer's own place first, then the places above it, nearest first), the rules with no place keep their order as before (Ordering, then the rule's number), and the two lists are taken together by Ordering, then number: a place rule never jumps ahead of a general rule with a lower Ordering and number than its own. A shop whose places are all countries prices exactly as before. The first "only this" rule in that order still applies alone, and combined and one-after-another rules still add up. The shipping taxes of an order follow the same order as its goods' taxes. A product's own price for a place still applies to that place only.

The product list sorts and filters a customer whose place is inside another by the same price the product page shows: it reads the figures prepared for the customer's own place, else for the nearest place above it that has discounts or taxes of its own, else the figures for no place. A new place inside a place with rules needs no rebuild. When a place is moved under another place, the product list's prices of the places below it are rebuilt in the background (Tools > Tasks) and the save says so.

A catalogue rebuild (Tools, Rebuild catalogue projections, and the background rebuild) no longer writes price figures for unpublished products, and removes those it finds, as unpublishing a product does. They were never shown, but took space and rebuild time.

The cart is priced at the place it is delivered to: once the checkout holds a delivery address (the country typed or chosen in the checkout, or, for a signed-in customer, their saved address that the checkout fills in by itself), the products in the cart, the coupon and the shipping charge are all priced for that place, on the cart page, after every change of address, in the cart module on every page and when the order is placed; the order builder's screen prices a customer's cart at its delivery place the same way, so staff see the total the order is placed at. Before, the products were priced at the visitor's own place (or at no place) while the shipping charge followed the address, so the same cart cost one amount in the shop and another when staff placed the order for the same address, and the builder's screen showed yet another. A place that is not published, or lies inside one that is not, prices as no place. Product lists and product pages keep showing the visitor's own prices; the cart page says "Prices are for delivery to" the place when it prices elsewhere.

An order is not placed at a total the shopper did not see: the cart page sends the total it shows with the order, and when the order's total differs (for example the address was changed in another tab), the order is refused with both totals and the shopper is shown the cart priced again. A template override of the cart's items layout (default_cart_items.php) made before 2.2.1 needs the new shown_total field, or orders through it are placed without this check; Joomla lists that override as changed after the update (Installer - Override).

REST API: a PATCH of an order (PATCH v1/alfa/orders/{id}) that carries a field the order's update does not write answers 422 naming it, and nothing is saved: reference, id_user, customer_name, customer_email, id_currency, currency, conversion_rate, delivery_date, id_address_delivery, id_address_invoice, id_payment_method, payment_method_name, id_shipment_method, shipment_method_name, status_name, payment_status, fulfillment_status, fulfillment_percentage, payment_percentage, balance, overpaid, excess, still_held, the totals (order_total, order_total_tax_excl, items_total, shipping_total, discount_total, contributions_total, total_paid_real, total_refunded_real), source, created, modified, lines, payments, shipments, contributions, history, delivery_address and invoice_address. An order's update writes its customer_note and its delivery and invoice details (alfa_form_fields, and alfa_form_fields_billing with invoice_differs); its status changes through POST v1/alfa/orders/{id}/status and its lines, payments and shipments through the order operations. Before, such a PATCH answered 200 and the order stayed as it was (payments and shipments answered 400 with a form message), except id_address_delivery and created, which were written as sent: an id_address_delivery could point the order at any address record, or at none, and a guest order then took that record's name and e-mail, so its next status e-mails went to that address; created took any date.

With Joomla's Shared Sessions on, a member of staff's own storefront session could reach an order they built for a customer in the order builder: the checkout details they had typed in their own storefront cart were read as the customer's delivery and invoice details by every plugin that reads the cart, the carriers' prices included, and a new cart the builder made for a customer was opened in the currency they had last chosen on the storefront. The order builder now reads none of the storefront's typed details, only the customer's own saved details and the place set in the builder, and opens a new cart in the shop's default currency, as it does without Shared Sessions.

An update of Alfa Commerce keeps a plugin of its package that staff disabled disabled (for example Web Services - Alfa Commerce, which closes the REST API, or the Standard payment or shipping plugin) and names it on the update page and in the maintenance log (com_alfa_maintenance.php). Before, every update enabled each of them again. A plugin the update installs for the first time is enabled; one whose install failed is not.

A product field whose plugin fails (for example an option type of another extension not built for this version) no longer takes down the product page, the cart page or the window that configures an order's product in the back office: the field is left out (a cart line shows it as its plain summary) and the failure is logged once in com_alfa_plugins.php. Before, the whole page failed, and no one could check out while the line was in a cart.

Adding a product to the cart writes the line and the options chosen for it together: if an option cannot be written (for example the database connection drops), the line is not added either and the shopper is told the add failed. Before, the cart could keep the product without some of its options, priced without their surcharges. Changing a line's options is the same: a failure leaves the line as it was.

An image refused when a product, category, manufacturer or variant is saved (not a valid image, or refused by a media plugin) no longer leaves a thumbnail of it in the images folder that no image uses.
A list of an extension's own screen in the back office that cannot be read shows an empty list and says so in plain words, the reason in com_alfa_panel.php, instead of PHP warnings or an error.

An installed search engine plugin that fails while giving its name or saying whether it is ready no longer stops the Options of Alfa Commerce from opening: it is listed as not ready, and the storefront searches the live catalogue.

The cart module reads nothing for a visitor who cannot have a cart yet (no account and no cart key in the browser): no database query for it on any page, for first-time visitors and crawlers alike, where it ran fifteen.

A form field's Layout setting (the layout its value is shown with in the order e-mails) is saved and used. Before, the choice was dropped when the field was saved, and the value was always shown with the default layout.

Tools > Extensions lists every plugin of another group (system, task, user, content and the others) that declares onClearData, whatever its namespace, with its Clear Data and the two Remove actions (each under its own permission and confirmation), and Clear everything calls it. Before, such a plugin was listed only when its namespace began with Alfa, so after Clear everything its data stayed while Alfa Commerce's was gone, and staff were not told. A plugin of another group whose code cannot be loaded is shown as could not be read, with the reason in the maintenance log, and Clear everything leaves it out. While Clear everything or a Clear Data is at work, the page no longer waits for it: it shows what it could read and says so.

Saving an order in the administrator keeps the order's own delivery details record: the id of that record, which the order screen sends as a hidden value, is no longer taken from the submitted page. Before, a changed id (a crafted request; the screen itself sends the right one) pointed the order at another customer's details record: a guest order then took that customer's name and e-mail, so its status e-mails went to them, and deleting the order deleted that customer's details. The details typed on the order screen are saved as before, also on an order that has no delivery details record yet.

The carriers that price by the shop's shipping zones (the Standard carrier, and carrier plugins that read the same zones) price a cart by the zone of the place nearest the delivery address: a zone for Crete before a zone for Greece for an address in Crete, wherever each sits in the list of zones; between zones for places at the same distance, the one higher in the list, as before. It is the order the discounts and taxes of a place follow. Before, the first zone in the list that covered the address won, so a zone for Greece listed above a zone for Crete charged an address in Crete the Greek price. The nearest zone decides alone: a cart none of its rows fit (too heavy for a Crete zone that goes up to 2 kg, for example) is refused by that carrier, not priced by the Greece zone, so give a narrower zone rows for every cart it should carry. A shop whose zones name countries only is priced as before.

An order whose shipping plugin recorded no parcel when it was placed (the plugin recorded none, its write failed, or it could not be loaded) gets its parcel from Alfa Commerce, with the shipping the customer was charged and every item, and a notification tells staff which shipping method recorded nothing and that a pickup point or locker the customer chose was lost with it and must be chosen again on the order's page. If Alfa Commerce cannot record it either, a notification tells staff that the order lacks its shipping charge and which charge to add by hand. Before, such an order lacked its shipping charge: once paid it read as overpaid by the shipping, and documents issued from it left the carriage out.

A shopper coming back from a payment provider or a carrier's pickup page whose plugin sends them nowhere lands on the cart with a message that the result could not be confirmed there, instead of an empty page. Coming back through a payment method that is disabled or missing, the message says that the payment method could not be identified, instead of "No order was specified".

After the customer's bank took a payment back (a lost dispute) or after a partial refund, the order can be paid again: a new payment for what the order is owed is accepted, through any payment method and from the order's page, and one beyond it is still refused. Before, it was refused, because the payment taken back still counted as paid. A payment or refund record the shop refuses no longer shows the shopper an internal message on the storefront; staff, and a REST client, get a plain sentence naming the order number.

A long run of the background work (the task runner started from the command line or a scheduler, a console command, a queue) reads the time again each time it needs it, instead of keeping the time it started at: a download granted later in the run is dated by its own grant and expires counted from it; a sales document issued later in the run is dated when it is issued (a run crossing midnight no longer dates the later documents the day before, nor a year-scoped series the first documents of a new year in the old year's numbering), and a series another request issued in meanwhile no longer refuses it with a clock error; a notification that expired during the run is no longer read as standing or kept by the clean-up, and one archived during the run expires counted from its own archiving; the product list's prices rebuilt during the run no longer count price, discount and tax dates already passed as still to come, which could leave a later start or end of a promotion out of the list's prices; and a stock movement recorded late in the run is no longer reported as stranded at once.

Invoicing an order in parts shares its discounts over the invoices by the value of the goods each one invoices, and a discount never reduces the shipping or the fees. Before, each discount on the document screen had its own tick, and the invoice that took the last goods claimed all that was left of a discount, out of the shipping when the goods were worth less: with a discount left off an earlier invoice, the last invoice could cancel its own shipping charge, state a negative VAT line at the goods' rate, and the invoices together came to more than the order. The discounts now have no tick: each invoice takes its share (20.34 of a 22.60 discount on an invoice of 101.70 of the order's 113.00 of goods, the rest on the last one), and the shipping and fees are invoiced as charged. Invoices already issued are not changed. Where an earlier invoice was issued without its share, the document screen says under the discount how much of it can no longer be claimed by an invoice, and that the order's invoices total that much more than the order until a credit note gives it back; an automatic issue of such an order's invoice says the same in the notifications and in the documents log. The part of a discount on the last invoice also carries the rest of the discount's net, so the invoices state its tax exactly as the order did. The two notices of an automatic issue that name an amount, shipping or fees on no document and discount no invoice can claim, state money as the other notifications do: in the currency's own format with its sign.

A product field extension that changes the parts of a catalogue card or of the order's item window and then fails no longer leaves its change on them: the card and the window are handed their parts once more after the last field, as the product page and the cart line already were.

The general subject of the status e-mails (used when a status leaves its subject empty), the same subject of the test e-mail, the test e-mail's list of orders and the message staff read when a payment record of an order is refused take the order's number from the one place that decides it, as the {order_number} token and the order-complete page do: the order's id, with no read of the order. Alfa Commerce never wrote an invoice number, so no number shown changes.

REST API: a PATCH of an order (PATCH v1/alfa/orders/{id}) that carries a field the order's update does not write answers 422 naming it, and nothing is saved: reference, id_user, customer_name, customer_email, id_currency, currency, conversion_rate, invoice_number, delivery_date, id_address_delivery, id_address_invoice, id_payment_method, payment_method_name, id_shipment_method, shipment_method_name, status_name, payment_status, fulfillment_status, fulfillment_percentage, payment_percentage, balance, overpaid, excess, still_held, the totals (order_total, order_total_tax_excl, items_total, shipping_total, discount_total, contributions_total, total_paid_real, total_refunded_real), source, created, modified, lines, payments, shipments, contributions, history, delivery_address and invoice_address. An order's update writes its customer_note and its delivery and invoice details (alfa_form_fields, and alfa_form_fields_billing with invoice_differs); its status changes through POST v1/alfa/orders/{id}/status and its lines, payments and shipments through the order operations. Before, such a PATCH answered 200 and the order stayed as it was (payments and shipments answered 400 with a form message), except id_address_delivery and created, which were written as sent: an id_address_delivery could point the order at any address record, or at none, and a guest order then took that record's name and e-mail, so its next status e-mails went to that address; created took any date.

A postcode written with spaces between its digits, as Greek postcodes are written (412 22), meets the Standard carrier's postcode band 41000 to 41999, as 41222 does, and both meet a band written the same way, 410 00 to 419 99: a postcode or a band limit made only of digits and spaces is read as its digits and compared as that number. A band may be whole postcodes or their first digits: 410 to 419 meets every postcode from 410 00 to 419 99, written with the space or without, and a lower or upper limit alone of three digits or more reads the postcode's first digits (up to 419 meets every postcode up to 419 99, from 410 every postcode from 410 00). A limit alone of one or two digits (a lower limit of 1 set to require a postcode) compares whole postcodes, as before. Before, "412 22" fell below a band written 41000 to 41999, "41222" fell outside one written 410 00 to 419 99, a band of first digits met only the spaced postcodes as their first digits read, and a band from 410 met every postcode written without the space (40999 among them). Limits of different lengths (41 to 419) compare as whole numbers. A postcode with a letter or a hyphen in it (UK, Canada, the Netherlands, US ZIP+4) is compared as before.

Deleting a place that has places inside it is refused, naming them, unless they are deleted with it: move them under another place first. Before, the places inside a deleted country became countries of their own, outside its discounts, taxes and carrier zones, and one inside an unpublished country could start to price.

A new shop no longer has the place Larisa inside Greece, a row of Alfa Commerce's own test data published in every installation up to 2.2.0. A shop that has it keeps it, since addresses, prices and rules may name it; the update names it and suggests, once Greece's regions are added, publishing Thessaly and then moving it under Thessaly (a place under an unpublished place is not offered at checkout), or unpublishing it.

An update to 2.2.1 adds the places' new ISO 3166-2 code column only where the table does not have it yet, so an update run again, or on a site whose database check already added the column, finishes without an error; the correction of the shop's countries during the update commits or rolls back the way Alfa's other saves do.

addition.item: REST API: more list filters, applied as the administrator's lists apply them. Orders: filter[payment] (paid, unpaid, failed or refunded; for failed and refunded the date window is on the payment's date, not the order's), filter[fulfilment] (shipped or unshipped), filter[waiting] (placed_48 or untouched_48), filter[reconciliation] and filter[overpaid] (on for 1 or true; 0, false or empty asks nothing), filter[date_start] and filter[date_end] (the order's date in the shop's time zone; an end date without a time includes that whole day), filter[item_id] (the orders of one product), and the customer: filter[id_user] (the customer's account; 0 lists the guests' orders) and filter[email] (the e-mail on the order, matched whole, letter case and accents aside, so a guest's orders are found too). Stock movements: filter[date_start] and filter[date_end] (as for orders) and filter[item_id] (the movements of one product). Documents: filter[date_start] and filter[date_end] (the document's date, both days included). Items: filter[stock] (in, low or out) and filter[fields] (filter[fields][field id][]=value id). An empty value asks nothing, a date that cannot be read is left out, and a filter a list does not have is ignored, as before. The orders table gains an index on the e-mail on the order, so the e-mail filter does not read every order.

After Alfa Commerce is installed or updated, the installation page, the maintenance log (com_alfa_maintenance.php) and one notification to the administrators name the installed Alfa Commerce extensions that are not known to work with it: those built for other versions of Alfa Commerce ("needs a compatible build") and those that do not say which versions they work with ("compatibility not stated"). Nothing is guessed from an extension's own version number. An Alfa Commerce extension here is one Tools > Extensions lists: a plugin of a group whose name begins with alfa or whose namespace begins with Alfa, or a module whose name begins with mod_alfa, so an extension of another vendor named that way is judged too. A recommended row of the setup checklist, Alfa extensions built for this version, names them until each one is updated to a build that says it works with this version; the notification is brought up to date as they are updated or removed. The extensions that ship with Alfa Commerce are never named.

For extension developers: an Alfa Commerce extension states the lines of Alfa Commerce it is built for in the manifest of each plugin and module it installs, as the element <alfacore min="2.2" max="2.2"/> beside its version (a line is a major and a minor version; the reader takes a range without max as every later line). Alfa Commerce reads it from those manifest files after its own update (a package's own manifest is not read there); an extension's install script reads the same element through AlfaInstallerGate::rangeRefusal(), which refuses an install outside the range in one wording, and AlfaCoreRange reads it for any other use. The Alfa extensions that ship with Alfa Commerce state 2.2; the easy articles module, which stands on its own, states none. An extension's own release adds the element to its manifest. The policy every Alfa extension follows: it declares both min and max, max being the last line it was tested on (2.2, never a patch release); one that installs on its own calls rangeRefusal() in its preflight, or refusal() with its own minimum where Alfa Commerce has no rangeRefusal() yet, so its install, update and discover_install are refused outside the range and its uninstall never is; a package declares the same range in its own manifest, which its installer hands to the gate, and in each plugin and module manifest it contains; and Alfa Commerce's own update is never refused because of an extension: after it, every installed Alfa extension outside its range or without one is named and keeps running.

For extension developers: AlfaPluginHelper::dispatchToIsolated() delivers an event to one plugin's declared handler and answers false when the handler throws, logged once per plugin and event in the request; a failure that ended the caller's transaction still reaches the caller. Core uses it for the item field plugins' surfaces on the product page, a cart line and the order's product window.

For extension developers: the carrier's onAdminOrderDelete event has getMethod(), the shipment the plugin is asked about, as the payment plugin's event has the payment. Before, a carrier reached the shipment only through getArgument('method').

The Alfa Dashboard's overview page carries a small Easylogic credit at its foot, linking to easylogic.gr. Its logo ships with Alfa Commerce, so the page asks nothing of another site, and it follows the administrator's light or dark colour scheme.

Two new ways to show a product's images. On the product page, Item Images offers Grid: every image at once, in 2, 3 or 4 columns (Images Grid Columns; two at most on a phone), each opening the lightbox. On the product list, the card's images are a part of their own, Items List Item Images: Default shows the first image as before, and Slider shows the product's first images (Images in the Card Slider: All, or 1 to 10) with arrows and dots; a swipe or a sideways scroll moves it without opening the product, a click on an image opens it, and it moves without animation for a visitor who asks for reduced motion. The three new settings are in the Options (Layouts), the product list's menu item (Layouts), the category and the product (both in their Layouts tab), and Images Grid Columns also in the product page's menu item; each level left empty takes the one above. The slider uses no library and shows the card's thumbnails, as the card did.

For extension developers: ShipmentsPlugin::amountToCollect() answers a carrier the amount still to collect on an order as Money, in the order's currency and never negative (what cash on delivery collects), so a carrier no longer reads PaymentLedger for it; PaymentLedger::amountToCollectMoney() is public. PaymentsPlugin::amountToCollect() and PaymentLedger::amountToCollect() still answer a float.

For extension developers: PaymentsPlugin gains bookedRefundable(), the books' refundable ceiling of an order as Money (PaymentLedger::bookedRefundable(), unchanged); ownMethods(), the plugin's own payment methods with their settings, published only by default; and the constant REFUND_BEYOND_PREFIX.

For extension developers: recordActionLog() on PaymentsPlugin and ShipmentsPlugin writes one row of Joomla's User Actions Log in the plugin's own words, filed under the plugin, and says whether it was written; ActionLogHelper::write() does the same for other code. There is no delete.

For extension developers: PaymentsPlugin::failRefundAttempt() (PaymentLedger::failRefundAttempt()) keeps a refund's reservation when the provider reports that one attempt failed and the request stands: the reservation gets a new key for the retry and no refundable figure moves, so the retry is not reserved a second time beside it. The same failure sent again answers OUTCOME_DUPLICATE; another gateway's payment is refused.

For extension developers: ChargeReferenceEvent carries the attempt number, getAttempt(), counted from 1 and set by the event's dispatcher, for a gateway's per-attempt idempotency key; a dispatcher that sets none dispatches attempt 1, and a value that is not an integer of at least 1 is refused.

For extension developers: PaymentsPlugin::authenticatedReturnFor(int $orderId) (final, public) is what a payment plugin calls from its browser return (onPaymentResponse) once it has authenticated the return for that order, in whatever session the return arrives and whatever the payment's result (paid, failed or cancelled by the buyer); the page before payment and the order page after it then show that order. Send a failed or cancelled return to the page before payment, which offers the retry; the order page after it offers none. A valid signed return link (orderFromReturnLink()) grants the same right as the method, so a return it authenticates may be marked. The method is idempotent, refuses an id below 1 with an InvalidArgumentException and reads no table. An order id a plugin writes into com_alfa.order_id itself is refused by both pages unless this session placed the order. A plugin built for 2.2.0 calls the method when it exists and keeps its own write.

Greece's 13 regions and Mount Athos, and the Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla inside Spain, come with a new shop as places inside their country, unpublished, named in English with their ISO 3166-2 codes. An existing shop adds them in Countries/States: select Greece or Spain and press Add subdivisions (codes already there are skipped; the update never adds them). Unpublished, they change nothing: no customer can pick one and nothing prices there. Once published, a country's discounts, taxes, shipping methods and carrier zones reach them, but a product's price for the country does not: a customer whose place is a region pays the product's price for that region, if it has one, otherwise its price for every place. The place's form says so.

A new shop has three more default fields in its customer details: Address, City and Postcode, required in the delivery section and optional at registration and in the invoice section, as couriers and sales documents need them. A new Standard shipping method's Postcode field setting starts on the Postcode field, so its postcode bands work as soon as the method has them.
